children: The Lean and Mathlib communities jointly announced that Levent Alpöge’s proof of the Riemann hypothesis had passed community verification. According to Odaily, Alpöge published the proof on November 20; written in Lean, it contains about 17 million lines of code. The communities said a day of intensive review confirmed that the statement of the proposition matches Mathlib’s definition of the Riemann hypothesis and that the proof is valid.

The review covered four areas: checking the proposition’s statement; confirming that the codebase compiles; using the independent tools comparator and con-leche –compare to verify that the theorem proved by the code matches Mathlib’s Riemann hypothesis; and checking the proof’s validity with Lean’s official kernel and other proof checkers, including con-leche and con-ron.

title: Lean and Mathlib Communities Verify Levent Alpöge’s Riemann Hypothesis Proof
